statement: A 2025/2026 study reports 13 additional fossil teeth from Ledi-Geraru showing Homo material at 2.78 and 2.59 million years ago and a new, unnamed Australopithecus species (not A. afarensis) at 2.63 million years ago, indicating early Homo and a distinct Australopithecus species co-existed at the same site 2.5-2.8 million years ago — alongside previously known Australopithecus garhi and Paranthropus material from the same general period in eastern Africa.

sources.citation: Reed, K.E. et al. "New discoveries of Australopithecus and Homo from Ledi-Geraru, Ethiopia." Nature 650: 374-380.
sources.author: Reed et al.

does_not_demonstrate: that Homo evolved from Australopithecus via a single linear replacement in this region

that only one non-Homo hominin lineage was present alongside early Homo in this period — at least three (this new species, A. garhi, Paranthropus) are attested in eastern Africa in the same broad window
